extracted.intended_audience: self-regulatory organizations (options exchanges) and their legal/finance teams preparing fee-change filings to the SEC (Rule 19b-4) / SEC staff reviewing such filings
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and justifying a proposed exchange fee (e.g., connectivity/port fees) to the SEC under the Exchange Act and the Revised Review Process, including cost allocations, competitive analysis, and member impact assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with section 6(b)(5) objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must be designed to "promote just and equitable principles of trade, remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general protect investors and the public interest" and not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers and dealers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the proposed fee furthers those statutory objectives; explain why it does not permit unfair discrimination. Use direct explanation of effects on market fairness and investor protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees must be reasonable, equitably allocated, and not unfairly discriminatory
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed fees must be "reasonable, equitably allocated, not unfairly discriminatory, and not an undue burden on competition."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence that the fee levels and allocation across participants satisfy these standards (e.g., comparisons, allocations by service, and showing no undue impact on particular classes of members).

rubrics_metrics.name: High standard of transparency and detailed justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges should meet very high standards of transparency to demonstrate why each new fee or fee amendment meets the Act's requirements that fees be reasonable, equitably allocated, not unfairly discriminatory, and not create an undue burden on competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comprehensive revenue and cost data and analysis, explain allocation methodologies, provide supporting quantitative information, and document the budget/process used to derive numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment whether fee is constrained by significant competitive forces
rubrics_metrics.description: As an initial step staff considers whether the fee is constrained by significant competitive forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include market-structure evidence (number of exchanges, alternatives like resellers/service bureaus, routing/sponsored access practices, elasticity of demand, market shares) demonstrating competitive constraints. If such forces operate, they provide a substantial basis for finding fees equitable and reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-based discussion as alternative when competitive constraints are insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: If an SRO cannot demonstrate that significant competitive forces constrain the fee, a cost-based discussion may be an alternative basis to show consistency with the Exchange Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a rigorous cost analysis, allocation of expenses to the service, and show how the proposed fee recovers those costs (with any proposed margin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specific quantitative information when supporting cost recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: If an SRO seeks to support its claims that a proposed fee is fair and reasonable because it will permit recovery of the SRO's costs, "specific information, including quantitative information, should be provided to support that argument."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply line-item annual and monthly costs, allocation percentages for cost drivers, demographic/usage data (number of ports/connections), and calculations showing aggregate costs and proposed revenue recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate parity/comparability with other exchanges' fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that proposed fees "promote parity among exchange pricing for access" and are similar to or less than fees charged for similar connectivity and port access by other options exchanges with comparable market shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a comparative table of competitor fees and market shares, cite filed fee schedules of other exchanges, and explain how parity promotes competition and affects ability to price transaction fees and invest in infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show that fee will not create undue burden on competition or smaller members
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully and transparently assess the impact on Members—both generally and in relation to other Members—to assure the fee will not create a financial burden on any participant and will not have an undue impact in particular on smaller Members and competition among Members in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze member-level impacts, provide examples of member departures or opt-outs, estimate elasticity for smaller firms, and demonstrate mitigations (e.g., free ports thresholds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document alternatives available to market participants (constraints on pricing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show availability of alternatives (not required to connect to every exchange): indirect connectivity via third-party resellers/service bureaus, sponsored access, routing to away markets, or choosing other exchanges constrains pricing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence (usage of resellers, membership statistics, routing behavior) that market participants can avoid direct connectivity and thus constrain an exchange's ability to charge high fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain business rationale for staged pricing for new entrants
rubrics_metrics.description: New exchanges often offer low or free connectivity initially to attract order flow and later amend fees to reflect the true value of those services after market share increases; allowing new entrants time to build market share before increasing fees encourages market entry and fee parity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe historical fee changes, timing relative to growth in market share, and show why phased pricing is reasonable and competitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a clear cost-allocation methodology and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt and document an allocation methodology (e.g., bottom-up departmental budgets, allocation of parent company costs to markets, then allocation to core services) developed through assessment by senior management, then reviewed and approved by senior finance executives and the Board/committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe each step of the methodology: department-level 'bottom up' budgets, Finance Team consolidation, CFO/CEO review, Board/Finance and Audit Committee approval, and principles guiding allocations (avoid double-counting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid double-counting and apply allocations consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure no cost is allocated twice or double-counted between the Exchange and its affiliated markets; apply allocation methodology consistently going forward for other fee proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how shared costs are partitioned, the logic for percentage splits, and commit to consistent future application; describe checks used to prevent duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide detailed line-item cost breakdowns with allocation percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: Disaggregate costs into line-items (Human Resources, connectivity external fees, Internet services/external market data, data center, hardware/software maintenance, depreciation, allocated shared expenses) and show allocated annual and monthly costs and percent of each cost driver related to the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present tables with annual and monthly figures, percentage allocations (e.g., 61.9% of data center), rounding conventions, and explanatory narrative for significant allocation choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute employee time to services for HR cost allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: For Human Resources, managers assign percentage of time for each employee among exchanges and then allocate employee time into buckets (connectivity, ports, market data, other services) so personnel costs are fully and appropriately allocated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe semi-annual or as-needed time-allocation processes, which departments/personnel are included (network infrastructure, systems ops, security, sales, finance), and provide the weighted-average percentages used (e.g., 42.4% allocated to 10Gb ULL connectivity for a certain group).

rubrics_metrics.name: Show aggregate cost, proposed fee, and resulting margin/recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate aggregate annual and monthly costs for the service (e.g., $11,361,586 annual for 10Gb ULL connectivity; $1,799,066 annual for MEI ports), propose fee levels (e.g., $13,500 per month per 10Gb connection), and explain that the fee covers costs and yields a modest profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show math tying allocated costs to proposed fee revenue, explain rounding conventions, and demonstrate the reasonableness of any modest margin claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain interdependence of revenue sources when allocating costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that exchanges have interdependent revenue sources (transaction fees, connectivity/port fees, membership, regulatory, market data) and that system components (connectivity, transaction execution, market data) are interdependent, requiring judgment in cost allocations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document how interdependencies were considered and the rationale for weighting allocations among services when no standardized methodology exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use empirical evidence of member behavior to support claims about elasticity and choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide data showing members' choices (e.g., membership decreases, number of firms accessing only one exchange, affiliate member overlap) to demonstrate that membership/connectivity is optional and that demand is elastic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite concrete examples (e.g., a Market Maker terminated membership due to proposed fees), membership statistics, and analyses showing number of exchanges used per firm to support the argument that high fees would deter participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain competitive impact of legacy exchanges' pre-existing fee baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that legacy exchanges often set higher non-transaction fees prior to Revised Review Process, creating an uneven playing field; explain how preventing non-legacy exchanges from raising non-transaction fees may hamper competitiveness (ability to subsidize transaction fees, invest in infrastructure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how non-transaction revenue can subsidize transaction fee reductions and fund investments, and show how fee constraints might disadvantage non-legacy exchanges competitively.
